subject: Computer's coded character set (whether UTF-8 or mixed alphanumeric and national characters recognized in class alphanum
notes: A.1 item 38 conditionally required. cite.py --check 8.3.3.2.3 "An implementation is neither required to recognize nor prohibited from recognizing UTF-8 or mixed alphanumeric and national characters" -> OK §8.3.3.2.3 2). cite.py --check 8.3.3.2.4 "the implementor shall specify the applicable general rules" -> OK §8.3.3.2.4 3) c). cite.py --check 8.1.2 "The implementor shall specify the set of characters in and the encoding of each of the computer's alphanumeric character set and the computer's national character set" -> OK §8.1.2 3). Determination follows R48's second section (alphanumeric set = the UTF-16 BMP): the doc-rows-1/d1 option (b) worry (a wide character in a PIC X literal being 'mixed' data behind a required user option) no longer exists, because every BMP character IS alphanumeric; the condition fails and the row documents non-provision. The code matches: VALUE "€é" in a PIC X(3) compiles clean at --std 2023 and holds U+20AC (i31.cob '8365 3 ...'); FUNCTION LENGTH("€é") = 2 (L38.cob) — the UTF-8 source bytes are decoded by SourceTextDecoder.Decode (read through CompilationInputs.ReadSourceText) before lexing. Witness l1c01_native_ordinal_positions_wide pins ORD("€") = 8365, i.e. the wide character is one alphanumeric position. pin 80de60472 (E:\wt\gl2-pin), out/run/d7: i31.cob (01 A PIC X(3) VALUE "€é"; DISPLAY ORD(A(1:1)) BYTE-LENGTH(A) CONVERT(A ANY ANUM HEX)) -> '8365 3 3FE920'; SQ7.cob (MOVE "€é" to a LINE SEQUENTIAL and a record SEQUENTIAL record, WRITE each with FILE STATUS) -> 'LS WRITE FS=00', 'SQ WRITE FS=00', sq7.dat = 3F E9 0D 0A, sq7r.dat = 3F E9 20 (U+20AC written as '?' with a successful status; kb/Work PB690 reproduces); L38.cob: FUNCTION LENGTH("€é") FUNCTION ORD("€") -> '2 8365'. retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Pipeline/CompilationInputs.cs#ReadAllText (CompilationInputs.ReadAllText no longer exists: the bytes of a source or library text become characters in SourceTextDecoder.Decode, read through CompilationInputs.ReadSourceText (kb/Work PB1397))
